INV-4 (secrets by reference) NOT-APPLICABLE: no secret material, no config, no env-var handling touched. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) NOT-APPLICABLE: no SQL, no Repo.query anywhere in this file. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) APPLIES, and is satisfied, not merely not-violated: the 3 added struct pattern matches (`%InstanceState{} = instance_state`, `%Token{} = token`) are call-boundary assertions inside a private function reachable ONLY from dispatch_node/4's own already-pattern-matched clauses, which themselves receive instance_state (narrowed at transition/3's own `%InstanceState{} = instance_state` head match) and token (returned by find_token/2 as a real Token.t() struct, since instance_state.tokens is always `[Token.t()]`) -- every real call path already supplies a well-formed struct at these positions, so the new pattern matches cannot raise a FunctionClauseError against any reachable caller. Confirmed by the full test suite staying green (761 passed, 0 failures, mix test re-run after this diff) -- no existing test path triggers a new crash. INV-2/INV-3/INV-5/INV-6's per-file 'once applicable' gates (S4/S5, new-data-access-path) do not apply -- no API route, no sandboxing surface, no new data-access path is introduced by this diff (INV-6 itself is the meta-invariant this handoff satisfies by existing).
